SUBJECT:  A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for
  periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration at 308 Descanso
  Avenue Upper (PC#2900)
________________________________________________________________________

SUMMARY: A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development
Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30)
consecutive days duration in the Multiple Residential – High Density (HD) zone at 308 Descanso
Avenue Upper. The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities). The
proposed project is not located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 25-62 approving a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2900 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a
authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit.

BACKGROUND:

Application Information:

  Applicant  Lanette Smith and Starla Broyles
  Owner  Terry Tuytens, Lanette Smith and Starla Broyles
  Location  308 Descanso Avenue Upper
  APN  7480-036-004
  General Plan  High Density Residential
  Land Use Designation
  Zoning Classification  Multiple Residential – High Density (HD)
  File Date  03/25/2025
   PC#2900 – 308 Descanso Avenue
  Page 2

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 308 Descanso Avenue. The
parcel is situated south of Beacon Street and north of Tremont Street. The lot is relatively flat,
with a gentle slope from west to east.

The project site is currently developed with a two-story duplex residence with two units, 308
Descanso Avenue (first floor unit) and 308 Descanso Avenue Upper (second floor unit). The
residential building is two stories, with a two bedroom unit with a kitchen, two bathrooms, a den
and a living room on the first floor, and an apartment with one bedroom, kitchen and a bathroom
on the second floor. The lower unit is full-time owner occupied by the property owner, and the
upper unit will be rented as a single unit. Originally constructed in 1919, the residence has had
several subsequent additions.

All abutting properties are in the HD zone and represent a mix of one- and two-story residential
buildings. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing short-term rental status,
is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

There are no entitlements previously granted for the project site.

The site has three different permits for home improvement:

  •  Permit #22102 – Rebuild second floor exterior staircase and handrails (2022)
   PC#2900 – 308 Descanso Avenue
  Page 3

  •  Permit #22178 – Replace sewer lateral (2022)
  •  Permit #23186 – Remodel upper unit bathroom and kitchen (2023)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicants, Lanette Smith and Starla Broyles, propose to short-
term rent the one-bedroom, one bathroom unit on the second floor of the residence, addressed
308 Descanso Avenue Upper. The building totals approximately 1,095 square feet in size, in
which the upper unit is approximately 275 square feet. The maximum occupancy of the unit will
be four (4) individuals based on the bedroom count and license limitations set forth in AMC
Section 3-1.317.g.

The proposed rental floor plan is included in Attachment 3 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: No issue items have been identified for the proposed project.
It is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately address
potential nuisance concerns related to transient rental, and no additional conditions are required
to meet the findings necessary to grant the TRL for the property.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant AMC Section 3-1.310 and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No.
PC 25-62 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy
The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion
of the residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in
Avalon Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses.
As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the
surrounding area.

Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the
exemptions as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2
and the Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for
   PC#2900 – 308 Descanso Avenue
  Page 4

the project. The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical
concern, does not result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the
environment due to unusual circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state
scenic highway, is not a hazardous waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: On December 5, 2025, the City sent a
Public Hearing Notice to owners/tenants within a 300-foot radius of the project site. The Hearing
Notice was published in Catalina Islander on December 5, 2025. The notice was posted at the
project site and in two additional locations on the same date.

ATTACHMENTS:

  1. Draft Resolution No. PC 25-62
  2. Vicinity Map
  3. Floor Plan
   PC#2900 - ATTACHMENT 1

DRAFT RESOLUTION NO. PC 25-62
   RESOLUTION NO. PC 25-62

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON APPROVING A TRANSIENT RENTAL LICENSE AND
  COASTAL DEVELOPMENT PERMIT FOR AN EXISTING APARTMENT
  UNIT LOCATED AT 308 DESCANSO AVENUE UPPER (PC#2900)

  WHEREAS, Lanette Smith and Starla Broyles (“Applicant”) filed an application
(“Application”) for a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit (PC#2900) to
allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration (“Project”) for the apartment unit located on the second floor of the duplex residential
building addressed 308 Descanso Avenue Upper, APN 7480-036-004 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a to review and take action on the subject applications for a Transient
Rental License and a Coastal Development Permit; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized High Density Residential by the General Plan Land
Use Element and is located within the designated area of the Multiple Family, High Density (HD)
zoning district as defined by AMC Section 9-5.406; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is within the planning
boundaries of the Avalon Local Coastal Program; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted one duly advertised public hearing on
December 17, 2025, at which time interested persons had an opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to granting a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit upon
property described in attached Exhibit “A”; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the approval of the Transient Rental License
and Coastal Development Permit have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon does hereby approve a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit to allow
renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration for the second floor apartment unit located at 308 Descanso Avenue Upper, based on the
following findings:

SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.
The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves

  1
 permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion of the
residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in Avalon
Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses. As such,
the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.
Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the exemptions
as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2 and the
Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for the project.
The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical concern, does not
result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual
circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state scenic highway, is not a hazardous
waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

SECTION 2 – FINDINGS

Transient Rental License
The proposed project may be granted a Transient Rental License for short-term rental per AMC
Chapter 3-1 (Business Licensing) Article 3 (Transient Rental Licenses). AMC Section 3-1.310 sets
forth the required findings for approval of a Transient Rental License as follows:
  a) The Planning Commission may, with such conditions as are deemed necessary, approve a
  Transient Rental License which will not jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger or
  otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general welfare, or be
  materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the vicinity of such use.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.

  b) In making such determination, the Planning Commission shall find that the proposed
  transient rental use is in general accord with the following principles and standards:

  1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where
  such use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses,
  buildings and structures;

  The subject property is an existing duplex residence with two attached units located
  within a predominantly residential area of the Flats. No modifications to the
  property are proposed that would alter the ability of the building or the unit to
  function as a residence in the future. The property was inspected by the Planning
  and Building Department prior to the public hearing and no health and safety issues
  were identified by the inspector that would prevent the residence from being used
  as a transient rental. Standard conditions of approval ensure that operation of the

  2
   transient rental will remain orderly and not have an adverse effect on surrounding
  residential properties.

  2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping,
  outdoor entertaining areas and other development features prescribed in this
  chapter or as required as a condition in order to integrate said use and not be
  detrimental with the uses in the neighborhood;

  The subject property has an existing two-bedroom, two bathroom multi-family unit
  on the first floor and a separate one-bedroom, one bathroom multi-family unit on
  the second floor. The area that will be approved for short term rental includes the
  second story unit with a kitchen, an indoor living area, and a bedrooms which will
  be accessible to transient guests. Pursuant to standard Condition #5, the property
  shall not provide a vehicle for the use of transient guests.

  3)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be served by highways and streets
  adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of
  traffic such use would generate.

  The project site is located on the east side of Descanso Avenue between Beacon
  Street to the north and Tremont Street to the south. This is a heavily traveled area
  by both vehicles and pedestrians, and Beacon Street and Tremont Street are
  identified as Major Circulation Facilities in the General Plan Circulation Element.
  It is anticipated that existing sidewalks and roadways, combined with the fact a
  vehicle will not be provided to transient guests, will ensure that traffic associated
  with operation of the business will not interfere with circulation along Descanso
  Avenue.

  4)  That the transient rental use must be ancillary to the residential use of residential
  unit, and would not create a commercial use in a residential zone. Whether a use
  is for a commercial use may be determined by the number of transient rental
  licenses previously granted to the applicant, the applicant's reason for the license
  and the nature of the requested license and any other factors presented in the
  application or at the hearing.

  The applicant currently does not operate any other transient rentals within the city.
  According to the owners, the property has been used as a full-time owner
  occupancy unit on the first floor and the upper unit has been vacant. No
  modifications are proposed to the residence to that would intensify the use of the
  property or alter the ability of the residential building or unit to function as a
  residence in the future.

c) Conditions imposed by the Planning Commission for a Transient Rental License may
  involve any pertinent factors affecting the establishment, operation and maintenance of the
  requested transient rental use, including, but not limited to:

  3
   1) Special yards, open spaces and buffer areas;
  2) Fences and walls;
  3) Parking facilities, including vehicular ingress and egress and the surfacing of parking
  area and driveways to specified standards;
  4) Street and highway dedications and improvements including sidewalks, curbs and
  gutters;
  5) Water supply and fire protection;
  6) Landscaping and maintenance of grounds;
  7) Regulation of nuisance factors such as noise, vibrations, smoke, dust, dirt, odors, gases,
  noxious matter, heat, glare, electromagnetic disturbances and radiation;
  8) Regulation of operating hours for activities affecting normal neighborhood schedules
  and functions;
  9) Regulation of signs, including outdoor advertising; and
  10) Such other conditions as will make possible the development of the proposed transient
  rental use in an orderly and efficient manner and in general accord with all elements
  of the General Plan and the intent and purpose of this chapter.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.

d) The Planning Commission shall deny the requested Transient Rental License where:

  1) The findings indicate, and the Commission determines, that the applicant has failed to
  show that the requested transient rental use will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use, and reasonable restrictions or conditions to license the
  establishment of the proposed use will not prevent detriment or menace as indicated.

  Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310.a-c, the required findings have been made to
  determine that the proposed transient rental will not jeopardize, adversely affect,
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use. Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth
  in AMC Section 3-1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No
  additional special conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the
  transient rental license operational regulations.

  2) The applicant fails to attend the hearing of the Planning Commission in person or
  virtually, unless a valid excuse is provided.

  The applicant confirmed with Staff their intent to be in attendance at the public hearing
  prior to the publication of the meeting agenda.

  4
   3) The applicant has previously had a Transient Rental License revoked for failure to
  maintain such license in good standing or for violation of the Municipal Code or any
  condition of the permit or had a conditional use permit revoked for violation of any
  requirement of this Municipal Code or violation of any condition of approval of the
  permit.

  The applicant has not had a business license, conditional use permit, or transient rental
  license for transient occupancy in the past, nor has any such license revoked for
  violations of the Municipal Code.

  4) The applicant previously operated a transient rental without a Transient Rental
  License. In deciding whether to deny the Transient Rental License on this basis, the
  Planning Commission may determine, in its reasonable discretion, whether substantial
  evidence supports that the applicant was not acting in bad faith when engaging in an
  illegal transient rental operation based upon: (1) the length of time that the operator
  failed to obtain a valid transient rental, (2) the length of time between when the
  operator was notified of the illegal operation and the time when the operator applied
  for a license, (3) whether the operator immediately discontinued illegal transient rental
  operation upon notice, (4) whether only one transient rental unit was operated, and (5)
  whether the operator was a sophisticated party, meaning the operator or its affiliates
  have engaged in transient rental operation previously. The applicant has the burden of
  presenting evidence that prior illegal transient rental operation was not conducted
  deliberately or in bad faith.

  The applicant has not previously operated a transient rental without a license within the
  City.

  5) The property proposed for transient rental use is out of compliance with any
  requirement of this Municipal Code at the time the Planning Commission hears the
  application.

  The project site is not subject to any active code enforcement cases and is otherwise in
  good standing with licensing and permitting requirements with the City of Avalon.

e) In addition to the foregoing, the Planning Commission shall consider the following in
  connection with an application for a Transient Rental License:

  1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed
  by the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has
  been rented for periods of more than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at any
  time during the two years preceding the application.

  5
   Staff has found no evidence that the subject property has been rented for 30 or more
  consecutive days or more to the same occupant in the last two years. According to the
  owners, the property has been used as a full-time owner-occupied home on the first
  floor, and the upper unit has been vacant.

2) Neighborhood Impacts. The Planning Commission shall consider the objections of the
  owners and occupants of neighboring properties in determining whether the proposed
  transient rental use is consistent with the surrounding properties and the extent to
  which such impacts may be mitigated by the imposition of the standard conditions listed

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located within the condominium building area of the Hamilton Cove
development. The unit is located adjacent to three multi-family condominium buildings and is the
only single-family residence in this area of the development. The building is situated between
Gaviota to the north and Playa Azul to the south. The lot slopes to the northeast towards
Hamilton Cove. Originally constructed in 1991, the residence has not been significantly modified
since it was completed.

All abutting properties are in the LD zone and represent a mix of residential condominiums within
Hamilton Cove. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing short-term rental
status, is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The project site was previously granted a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) (PC#1684) for short-
term rental of the property. However, AMC Section 3-1.315 limits the transferability of transient
rental CUPs to a one-time transfer, subject to specific qualifications. For this property, the CUP
did not transfer to the current owners as there were multiple previous property sales which led
to the expiration of the CUP.

The property does not have any recent or active building permit history.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicant, Anita Petersen, proposes to short-term rent a four
bedroom, four and a half bathroom single-family residence. The residence is three stories, with
interior living space and an unenclosed deck. The entire residence will be rented as a single unit.
The residence is approximately 3,542 square feet in size. The maximum occupancy of the unit
will be ten (10) individuals based on the bedroom count and license limitations set forth in AMC
Section 3-1.317.g.

The transient rental floor plan is included as Attachments 3 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: No issue items have been identified for the proposed project.
The residence is located within the condominium area of Hamilton Cove, but the unenclosed
decks and primary living areas do not directly face the outdoor living areas of any of the adjacent
condominium buildings. It is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions
adequately address potential nuisance concerns related to transient rental, and no additional
conditions are required to meet the findings necessary to grant a TRL for the property.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant AMC Section 3-1.310 and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No.
PC 25-63 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy
The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion
of the residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in
Avalon Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses.
As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the
surrounding area.

Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the
exemptions as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2
and the Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for

  FAMILY RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 56 GAVIOTA (PC#2901)

  WHEREAS, Anita Petersen (“Applicant”) filed an application (“Application”) for a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit (PC#2901) to allow renting or leasing
of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration (“Project”) for
the single-family residence located at 56 Gaviota, APN 7480-048-110 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a to review and take action on the subject applications for a Transient
Rental License and a Coastal Development Permit; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized Low Density Residential by the General Plan Land
Use Element and is located within the designated area of the Low Density Residential (LD) zoning
district; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is within the planning
boundaries of the Avalon Local Coastal Program; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted one duly advertised public hearing on
December 17, 2025, at which time interested persons had an opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to granting a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit upon
property described in attached Exhibit “A”; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the approval of the Transient Rental License
and Coastal Development Permit have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon does hereby approve a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit to allow
renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration of the single-family residence located at 56 Gaviota, based on the following findings:

SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.
The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves
permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion of the
residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in Avalon

  1
 Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses. As such,
the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.
Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the exemptions
as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2 and the
Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for the project.
The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical concern, does not
result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual
circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state scenic highway, is not a hazardous
waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

SECTION 2 – FINDINGS

Transient Rental License
The proposed project may be granted a Transient Rental License for short-term rental per AMC
Chapter 3-1 (Business Licensing) Article 3 (Transient Rental Licenses). AMC Section 3-1.310 sets
forth the required findings for approval of a Transient Rental License as follows:
  a) The Planning Commission may, with such conditions as are deemed necessary, approve a
  Transient Rental License which will not jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger or
  otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general welfare, or be
  materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the vicinity of such use.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.

  b) In making such determination, the Planning Commission shall find that the proposed
  transient rental use is in general accord with the following principles and standards:

  1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where
  such use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses,
  buildings and structures;

  The subject property is an existing single-family residence located within the
  Hamilton Cove condominium development. No modifications to the property are
  proposed that would alter the ability of the building to function as a single-family
  residence in the future. The property was inspected by the Planning and Building
  Department prior to the public hearing and no health and safety issues were
  identified by the inspector that would prevent the residence from being used as a
  transient rental. Standard conditions of approval ensure that operation of the

  2
   transient rental will remain orderly and not have an adverse effect on surrounding
  residential properties.

  2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping,
  outdoor entertaining areas and other development features prescribed in this
  chapter or as required as a condition in order to integrate said use and not be
  detrimental with the uses in the neighborhood;
  The subject property is an existing four bedroom, four and a half bathroom single-
  family residence. The residence includes kitchen, indoor living area, and exterior
  decks which will all be accessible to transient guests. The property will offer a
  vehicle for transient rental guests, which has a designated off-street parking space.

  3)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be served by highways and streets
  adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of
  traffic such use would generate.
  The project site is located between Gaviota and Playa Azul within the Hamilton
  Cove residential development. Hamilton Cove is a gated community, with access
  only granted to residents and guests, which limits the amount of pedestrian and
  vehicular traffic to the area. St. Catherine Way, the only road access from Hamilton
  Cove to the city center, is not identified as a Major Circulation Facility in the
  General Plan Circulation Element. A vehicle will be provided for transient guests,
  which will ensure that transient guests will have adequate access to amenities and
  services within the city center of Avalon.

  4)  That the transient rental use must be ancillary to the residential use of residential
  unit, and would not create a commercial use in a residential zone. Whether a use
  is for a commercial use may be determined by the number of transient rental
  licenses previously granted to the applicant, the applicant's reason for the license
  and the nature of the requested license and any other factors presented in the
  application or at the hearing.
  The applicant currently does not own any other transient rentals within the city.
  According to the owners, the property has been used as a part-time owner-occupied
  vacation home. No modifications are proposed to the residence that would
  intensify the use of the property or alter the ability of the residence to function as a
  single-family condominium residence in the future.

c) Conditions imposed by the Planning Commission for a Transient Rental License may
  involve any pertinent factors affecting the establishment, operation and maintenance of the
  requested transient rental use, including, but not limited to:

  3
   1) Special yards, open spaces and buffer areas;
  2) Fences and walls;
  3) Parking facilities, including vehicular ingress and egress and the surfacing of parking
  area and driveways to specified standards;
  4) Street and highway dedications and improvements including sidewalks, curbs and
  gutters;
  5) Water supply and fire protection;
  6) Landscaping and maintenance of grounds;
  7) Regulation of nuisance factors such as noise, vibrations, smoke, dust, dirt, odors, gases,
  noxious matter, heat, glare, electromagnetic disturbances and radiation;
  8) Regulation of operating hours for activities affecting normal neighborhood schedules
  and functions;
  9) Regulation of signs, including outdoor advertising; and
  10) Such other conditions as will make possible the development of the proposed transient
  rental use in an orderly and efficient manner and in general accord with all elements
  of the General Plan and the intent and purpose of this chapter.

  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.

d) The Planning Commission shall deny the requested Transient Rental License where:

  1) The findings indicate, and the Commission determines, that the applicant has failed to
  show that the requested transient rental use will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use, and reasonable restrictions or conditions to license the
  establishment of the proposed use will not prevent detriment or menace as indicated.

  Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310.a-c, the required findings have been made to
  determine that the proposed transient rental will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use. Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals as set forth
  in AMC Section 3-1.317 have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No

  2) The applicant fails to attend the hearing of the Planning Commission in person or

  4
   The applicant confirmed with Staff their intent to be in attendance at the public hearing
  prior to the publication of the meeting agenda.

  3) The applicant has previously had a Transient Rental License revoked for failure to
  maintain such license in good standing or for violation of the Municipal Code or any

  The applicant has not had a business license, conditional use permit, or transient rental

  4) The applicant previously operated a transient rental without a Transient Rental

  illegal transient rental operation based upon: (1) the length of time that the operator
  failed to obtain a valid transient rental, (2) the length of time between when the
  operator was notified of the illegal operation and the time when the operator applied
  for a license, (3) whether the operator immediately discontinued illegal transient rental

  whether the operator was a sophisticated party, meaning the operator or its affiliates

  presenting evidence that prior illegal transient rental operation was not conducted

  The applicant has not previously operated a transient rental without a license within the
  city.

  5) The property proposed for transient rental use is out of compliance with any

  The project site is not subject to any active code enforcement cases and is otherwise in
  good standing with licensing and permit requirements with the City of Avalon.

e) In addition to the foregoing, the Planning Commission shall consider the following in
  connection with an application for a Transient Rental License:

  1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed
  by the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has
  been rented for periods of more than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at any

   Staff has found no evidence that the subject property has been rented for 30 consecutive
  days or more to the same occupant in the last two years. According to the owners, the

2) Neighborhood Impacts. The Planning Commission shall consider the objections of the
  owners and occupants of neighboring properties in determining whether the proposed

3) Condominium Associations Having 10 or More Units. In the case of an application
  concerning property located within a condominium or similar congregate housing
  project consisting of 10 or more units, the applicant shall be required to provide written

  allowance of the transient rental use at the condominium or congregated housing

  The applicant has received approval from the Hamilton Cove Homeowners Association
  for transient rental of the property, conditioned upon compliance with the City’s TRL

4) The Planning Commission shall consider whether granting the Transient Rental
  License shall result in any year round residence located adjacent to the proposed
  transient rental having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or
  licensed for transient rental use. "Adjacent" means having a common property line with
  the proposed transient rental unit except for the existence of a public street or alley.
  The total square footage of the dwelling unit and the site of each bedroom shall be
  considered for determining whether to grant the Transient Rental License.

  Due to the unique layout of the Hamilton Cove condominiums, with clusters on units
  within detached buildings, adjacent residences have been defined based on adjacent
  units within the same condominium building. The subject property is located adjacent
  to Buildings 11, 13, and 18 of the Hamilton Cove development.

  6
   The vicinity map prepared for the project, included as Attachment 2 of the staff report,

  The subject property is approximately 3,542 square feet in size, which is within the
  average size range for a single-family condominium units and standalone residences in

  and the placement of the bedrooms does not provide cause for concern with granting

  f) The Planning Commission shall impose as a condition all of the requirements and

  Required and recommended conditions of approval have been included as an attachment

Coastal Development Permit
The City of Avalon is located entirely within the Coastal Zone. The project is located within the
300-foot appealable boundary of the Coastal Zone and qualifies as an increase in the intensity of
use that requires issuance a Coastal Development Permit per AMC Section 9-8.102.b.2.v, on the
following findings:
  1. The use is in conformance with the certified Local Coastal Program. (AMC 9-
  8.103.d.1)

  Determination of conformance for projects within the City of Avalon includes analysis of
  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances, as
  applicable.

  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The Low Density Residential (LD) zoning
  designation of the project site is consistent with the General Plan land use designation
  of Low Density Residential.

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies:

  Policies II-20 and II-21 of the Land Use Element:

  7
   “Pursue new developments and businesses that add to the City’s economic base,
  particularly those that general sales tax and transient occupancy tax.”

  “Expand lodging choices by attracting and retaining desirable and high-quality
  facilities to the community.”

  The City recognizes that short-term rentals contribute significantly to economic
  development and allow visitors to experience the unique island community of Avalon
  and assist in providing access to the coast. Permitting and regulation of short-term
  rentals through the Transient Rental License process allows the City to monitor rental
  activity to ensure their operation has minimal negative impact to surrounding properties
  and also provides a significant income from transient occupancy tax, which is paid
  monthly to the City.

  •  Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP): The Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP)
  emphasizes the fact that Avalon is a visitor-focused community, with multiple visitor-
  serving facilities and recreational opportunities. Availability of short-term rentals
  provides access to alternative forms of accommodation for visitors to the community
  within existing developed properties, supplementing the need for new visitor-serving
  development. Continued permitting and management of short-term rentals in the
  community is consistent with the intent of the LCP and implements Sections 30213 and
  30222 of the California Coastal Act.

  •  LD Zone Development Standards: The proposed project does not involve any
  modifications or additions to an existing building that require analysis pursuant to the
  development standards for the LD zone. No adjustments or variances are required to
  permit the proposed project.

  •  Affordable Housing Ordinance: This ordinance is not applicable to the proposed project
  since the proposal does not include the development of five or more residential units.

2. For all development seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, the
  proposed development conforms to the public access and recreation policies of
  Chapter 3 of the Coastal Act. (AMC 9-8.103.d.2)

  The project site is not seaward of Gaviota which is the nearest roadway access to the
  shoreline relative to the location of the project site. The proposed project involves
  permitting short-term rental use of an existing developed residential property in a
  residential area of the city, in compliance with development standards for the LD zone and
  Transient Rental License regulations. Therefore, the project does not involve a change in
  land use, density, or intensity that will result in increased demand for public access and
  recreation opportunities. Furthermore, the project does not include any building or site
  modification that could block or impede existing public access opportunities.

  8
 Annual Growth Policy
The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

SUMMARY: A Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development
Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30)
consecutive days duration in the Multiple Residential, High Density (HD) zone at 131 Hill Street
Unit B. The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality
Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities). The proposed
project is not located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 25-64 approving a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2902 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a
authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit.

BACKGROUND:

  Applicant  Scott and Allyn Bryan
  Owner  Bryan, Scott W and Allyn R TRS Bryan Family Trust

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a rectangular flag lot addressed 131 Hill Street. The parcel is
situated south of Chimes Tower Road and north of Hill Street. The lot slopes towards the east.
Access to the building is located on Chimes Tower Road.

The project site is currently developed with two units, connected with attached walkways. The
main residence (131 Hill Street) is a three-story residential building. The subject property is an
apartment (131 Hills Street) located on the 2nd floor of the attached accessory building, which
also includes the garage on the top floor (at street level) and a shop room below.

All abutting properties are in the HD zone and represent a mix of single and multi-story residential
buildings. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing short-term rental status,
is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The following entitlements have been previously granted for the project site:

  •  PC# 2266 – Approval of a Variance and Coastal Development Permit for demolition and
  construction of a single-family residence and apartment.
   PC#2902 – 131 Hill Street Unit B
  Page 3

There are no active or recent building permits for this property.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicant, Allyn Bryan, proposes to short-term rent a one
bedroom, one bathroom apartment unit. The unit is approximately 484 square feet in size and is
located on the 2nd floor of the accessory building on the property. An unenclosed balcony is
accessible from the living room. The entire unit will be rented as a single unit. The maximum
occupancy of the unit will be four (4) individuals based on the bedroom count and license
limitations set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317.g.

The main residence will remain as an owner-occupied dwelling unit.

The transient rental floor plan is included as Attachment 3 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: No issue items have been identified for the proposed project.
It is the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately address
potential nuisance concerns related to transient rental, and no additional conditions are required
to meet the findings necessary to grant a TRL for the property.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant AMC Section 3-1.310 and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No.
PC 25-66 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy

The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion
of the residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in
Avalon Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses.
As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the
surrounding area.

  8.103.d.1)

  Determination of conformance for projects within the City of Avalon includes analysis of
  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances, as
  applicable.

  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The Multiple Family, High Density (HD) zoning
  designation of the project site is consistent with the General Plan land use designation
  of High Density Residential.

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies:

  Policies II-20 and II-21 of the Land Use Element:

  “Pursue new developments and businesses that add to the City’s economic base,
  particularly those that general sales tax and transient occupancy tax.”

  7
   “Expand lodging choices by attracting and retaining desirable and high-quality
  facilities to the community.”

  The City recognizes that short-term rentals contribute significantly to economic
  development, allow visitors to experience the unique island community of Avalon, and
  assist in providing access to the coast. Permitting and regulation of short-term rentals

  to ensure their operation has minimal negative impact to surrounding properties and
  also provides a significant income from transient occupancy tax, which is paid monthly
  to the City.

  •  Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP): The Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP)

  provides access to alternative forms of accommodation for visitors to the community
  within existing developed properties, supplementing the need for new visitor-serving
  development. Continued permitting and management of short-term rentals in the
  community is consistent with the intent of the LCP and implements Sections 30213 and
  30222 of the California Coastal Act.

  •  HD Zone Development Standards: The proposed project does not involve any
  modifications or additions to an existing building that require analysis pursuant to the
  development standards for the HD zone. No adjustments or variances are required to
  permit the proposed project.

  2. For all development seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, the

  Chapter 3 of the Coastal Act. (AMC 9-8.103.d.2)

 fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing

SUBJECT:  A Public Hearing and consideration of a resolution recommending
  approval of the 2026 Annual Growth Policy to the City Council as required
  by Avalon Municipal Code Section 9-12.102 (PC#2897)
________________________________________________________________________

SUMMARY: A Public Hearing and consideration of a resolution recommending approval of
the 2026 Annual Growth Policy to the City Council as required by Avalon Municipal Code
Section 9-12.102, finding the effects and demands of development permitted in the City over
the preceding ten months (January 1 – October 31, 2025) in compliance with all applicable
regulations and exempt from environmental review under the CEQA "General Rule" Section
15061(b)(3).

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find the project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15061(b)(3); and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 25-60 recommending City Council adopt a resolution
  approving the 2026 Annual Growth Policy (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: AMC Section 9-12.102 authorizes the Planning Commission to
review and take action on recommendations to the City Council on the Annual Growth Policy.

BACKGROUND: Section 9-12.102 of the Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) stipulates that the
City Council, in conjunction with the Planning Commission, shall review the growth permitted
in the preceding ten months, review the effects and demands of such development and any
additional development upon the City's natural resources, and determine, by resolution, the
amount and type of growth the City will permit in the succeeding year, as well as City
priorities for growth.

A summary of local development activity during the past year (January 1 through October 31,
2025) has been tabulated and is attached as "Exhibit A" to the proposed Resolution No. PC
25-60 (Attachment 1) .

DISCUSSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS:

Water Allocation Status:
Southern California Edison (SCE) is not currently in any stage of water rationing. Fresh
water allocations assigned to applicants on the Fresh Water Allocation List will be honored
and a waiting list has been established for projects pending availability of new freshwater
allocation (Attachment 2). However, at this time no new freshwater allocations will be
   PC#2897 – 2026 Annual Growth Policy
  Page 2

assigned until SCE completes construction of Phase II of the desalination system
expansion, with an estimated completion at the end of 2026. Once construction is complete,
a water availability assessment will be completed to determine the available water supply
and potential water surplus. SCE will notify the City once the assessment is complete with
an anticipated timeline for when water will be available for new allocations.

Recommendations:
Staff recommends maintaining the Annual Growth Policy development limits as they were
approved for the 2025 calendar year. A development project shall only be required to fall into
one of the foregoing categories to qualify for consideration. The permitted classes of projects
are set forth in greater detail in Attachment 1.

  •  The repair, in-kind replacement, remodeling or enlargement of existing commercial
  and residential structures, subject to specified conditions;

  •  In-fill projects involving limited new construction and subject to specified conditions;

  •  Residential tract development, if specified conditions can be met;

  •  ADUs or JADUs are allowed as provided in Article 6 of Chapter 9-5 of the Avalon Municipal
  Code if the water provider indicates there is sufficient water by issuing a water
  allocation or indicates that no allocation is needed;

  •  Infrastructure projects authorized by the City/Successor Agency;

  •  Projects which the Planning Commission determines will not have growth inducing
  effects; and

  •  Projects which are not in-fill in nature or involve existing residential or commercial
  structures but for which CEQA documents have been adopted and findings made that
  explain why the resulting growth is beneficial to the City and its residents.

Almost all of the above development categories require confirmation from SCE that
adequate fresh water is available to support the proposed project. Planning staff continues
to coordinate with SCE regarding review of new planning applications within the city.
Potential development applications that staff are aware of are reflected on the current SCE
waitlist and/or would fall into one of the above development categories. Therefore, if a water
allocation becomes available in 2026, entitlements for these projects would not be delayed
by the implementation of the Annual Growth Policy as recommended.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

The Avalon General Plan recognizes the need to minimize water consumption in light of limited
water resources available on the island. The Land Use Element, Housing Element, and
Conservation Element set forth goals and policies which balance community growth and
protection of natural resources through organized development practices. The Annual Growth
Policy is also incorporated as an integral part of the City’s certified Local Coastal Program (LCP)
Implementation Plan.
   PC#2897 – 2026 Annual Growth Policy
  Page 3

Annual review and update of the Annual Growth Policy allows the City to adapt to changing
availability of water resources while providing the community with direction to plan for future
development projects. Therefore, the proposed policy is in compliance with both the Avalon
General Plan and the Local Coastal Program.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed policy is exempt from the provisions of
the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15601(b)(3)
because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment and is not subject to
CEQA.

The proposed policy establishes standards for the approval of allowed growth within the
parameters of existing General Plan and municipal code regulations. It does not authorize
any changes to land use limitations or approve any new development project. Therefore,
there is no reasonable possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect
on the environment.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The Hearing Notice was published in
Catalina Islander on December 5, 2025. The Hearing Notice was posted in three location(s) on
the same date.

  writing that water is available to serve the project, if approved by the City. As used herein,

  not prohibit consideration and approval of conditional use permits for transient occupancy,

  footage by <50%; or
  iii.  any expansion of existing recreational/visitor serving development, not over 5,000

Existing Site:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel at 305 Beacon Street. The parcel is
situated near the southeast corner of Metropole Avenue and Beacon Street. Metropole Avenue
slopes steeply southeasterly to northeasterly from Tremont Street (south) toward Beacon Street
(north). Beacon Street slopes northwesterly from Calle Del Sol (northwest) to southeasterly
(Sumner Avenue).

The project site is currently developed with a single-story, three bedroom single-family
residence. The Los Angeles County Assessor shows the year built as 1953, but a residence has
been shown at the property as far back as 1891 per historic Sanborn Fire Insurance maps. The
residence is designed in a simple vernacular style, constructed of concrete block with a low
pitched gable roof. There is one small tree at the rear of the building, and minimal non-native
shrubs on the rest of the property.

The existing residence was occupied by members of the Cameron family. However, it has been
vacant since approximately 2000 and has fallen into a state of disrepair. The building does not
meet current building code standards and has been utilized as storage since the last time it was
occupied.

All abutting properties are in the Special Commercial zone and represent a mix of commercial,

east, multi-family housing to the south (310 Metropole Avenue), the Cameron Hotel (301 Beacon
Street, under construction), and the Hotel St. Lauren (231 Beacon Street) to the west.

demolish an existing single-family residence and construct a new two-story hotel with employee

and a rooftop deck with an elevator, bathroom and pool.

Hotel rooms will be offered for rent on a daily basis, consistent with standard hotel operations.
The rooftop pool area will be open from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily and accessible only to adult

The application proposes that the project will operate in concert with the Cameron Hotel (301

The applicant proposes that shared hotel operations will allow for eﬃcient 24-hour on-site

In addition, a 10-foot wide shared access easement will be established across the rear of 301

The proposed project has been designed to maintain separate property ownership of each parcel

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: Staff have identified five issues for discussion regarding the
proposed project.

Issue 1: Variances from Development Standards

The applicant is requesting multiple variances from the development standards for the SC zone,
as follows:

  •  Allow building height of 18 to 30 ft above grade to top of parapet, with an additional 10 ft
  for rooftop bathroom enclosure, 12 feet for elevator tower, and 16 feet for emergency
  staircase, where 28 feet is allowed. A building height diagram is included as Attachment
  6.
  •  Allow 93% lot coverage, where a maximum of 80% is allowed.
  •  Allow 166% floor area, where a maximum of 140% is allowed.

Per AMC Chapter 9-8.405, variances from development standards may be permitted by the
Planning Commission where the special circumstances may deprive a property of privileges
enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning classification, the property is
not granted special privileges beyond those available to similar properties, does not permit a use
that is otherwise not allowed, and complies with the Avalon Local Coastal Program.

Though the property is of regular size, the sloped topography of the lot is unusual compared to
the majority of other properties within the SC zone. The majority of lots within the Special
Commercial zone, and commercial zoning districts in general, are located within the “Flats”. As
a result, the development standards have been written to apply to lots with flat topography. For
instance, the maximum building height in the SC zone is 28 feet. The municipal code definition
for building height is “…the vertical distance from the lot's natural surface to the highest point of
the building.” (AMC Section 9-3.608). Other zones in the city, particularly the residential zones,
have additional detailed standards for measurement of building height (low slope, hillside, steep
hillside) that account for the topography present within the zone to allow for equitable
development of all lots. However, in the case of a sloped lot in the SC zone strict application of
the definition of building height would mean that the actual buildable area of the lot would be
substantially less on a sloped lot than a flat lot, which would deprive the property of the same
development potential compared to other properties within the same zone.

The requested variances are consistent with approved development of other properties with
hotels on sloped lots within the immediate vicinity of the project. The Hotel St. Lauren (231
Beacon Street), Casa Maraquita (229 Metropole Avenue), and the Cameron Hotel (301 Beacon
Street) are hotel projects also developed in the SC zone under the same development standards
which exceed development standards, including height, floor area, and lot coverage standards
for the zone. According to the permitting records for these projects, approval was granted
   PC#2887 – 305 Beacon Street
  Page 7

because of the topography of the lots, and with acknowledgement that while the hotels were
larger than permitted by the development standards for the zone, they fit within the context of
the existing development and topography in the surrounding area.

Therefore, it is the opinion of staff that the proposed variances may be granted in conformance
with the findings of the municipal code, as there are special circumstances related to lot
topography that would otherwise deprive the property of the development potential of other flat
lots within the same zone, and the variances do not constitute granting of special privileges and
similar variances have previously been granted for the same use on similarly sloped lots within
the same zone.

Issue 2: Operational Coordination with 301 Beacon Street

A 10-foot wide shared access easement is proposed across the rear of 301 Beacon Street to
allow to access to the proposed commercial autoette parking space and trash enclosure at the
rear of the project site from Metropole Avenue. Without this access easement, the applicant
would not have access to rear the property, as the side setbacks are proposed to be 0 ft on both
sides of the building.

Both 301 and 305 Beacon Street are controlled by members of the same family, and the
applicant has established long-term leases for construction and operation of a shared hotel
between the two parcels. Therefore, it is the opinion of staff that it is feasible for the applicant to
obtain the easement to ensure conformance with the trash enclosure and parking requirements
of the municipal code.

Staff recommends Condition #4 of the draft resolution, which shall require the applicant to obtain
the legal access easement between the two parcels prior to issuance of permits for the proposed
project. The City shall be required to sign off on any transfer or abandonment of the easement
to ensure the operation of the site continues to comply with all conditions of approval in the
future.

Issue 3: Employee Housing

AMC Section 9-11.104.d requires that any new commercial development shall provide rental
housing for at least 50% of the peak season employees. The applicant has estimated that one
full-time employee will be employed by the business with the completion of both phases of the
project. The proposed project shall provide housing for one employee, consisting of one
housekeeper studio units on-site, which exceeds the housing requirements of the municipal
code.

Combined with 301 Beacon Street, the shared operations would employ approximately five full-
time employees and provides four on-site employee housing units.

There is no standard unit size requirement for employee housing units. However, all rentals must
be for the period of not less than six months to provide for housing stability for employees. Rents
for such accommodations may be established by the hotel operator with City approval.

The proposed project is subject to audit by the City following the first peak season after
commercial operations have commenced to ensure that a sufficient amount of employee housing
has been provided to accommodate at least 50% of peak season employees. The City reserves
   PC#2887 – 305 Beacon Street
  Page 8

the right to modify the new commercial development's rental space requirements in line with
municipal code requirements if the estimation in this application is deficient.

Issue 4: Rooftop Deck Operations

According to the applicant, the rooftop deck will be a gathering place for hotel guests to sit and
enjoy the views of Avalon Bay and the surrounding hillsides. The rooftop deck is designed with
a 68 SF bathroom building and a 492 SF pool. The rooftop deck will be open from 7:00 AM until
10:00 PM. Any special event held on the deck would require a Special Event Permit (AMC
Chapter 4-6) and demonstrate compliance with all city code requirements.

Use of the rooftop deck has the potential to create noise nuisance for surrounding properties.
Operations must be consistent with Avalon Municipal Code Section 5-13.08 for a building within
Noise District 3, which states that it is “unlawful to use or operate or cause to be used or operated
outdoors any radio receiving set, sound amplifying equipment, television set, or other machine
or device which produces or reproduces sound in such a manner as to be plainly audible from
the real property line on which the sound amplifying equipment is located unless permitted by
Special Use Permit.” The applicant is not requesting approval of a Special Use Permit at this
time.

It is the opinion of staff that with limited hours of operation, restriction allowing only adult guest
access, and the requirement for a Special Event Permit for events, the proposed roof deck is
compatible with the intent of the SC zone and should not cause undue noise nuisance to
surrounding properties. The roof deck is surrounded by a glass railing along the parapet wall,
and the rooftop kitchen and mechanical equipment building is placed to provide separation
between the deck and adjacent residential uses to the east and south.

This conclusion is further supported by the Noise Impact Analysis prepared for the project,
provided as Appendix B of Attachment 7 of this report. The report calculated potential noise
levels for operation of 305 Beacon Street, and a cumulative calculation with the roof deck at 301

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15332 (Class 32 – In-fill Development Projects) because it has no potential to have a significant
effect on the environment.

The Class 32 reflects a determination by the California Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
that projects that meet the Class 32 criteria will not have a significant environmental effect and,
therefore, are exempt from CEQA. (Berkeley Hillside Preservation v. City of Berkeley (2015) 60
Cal.4th 1086, 1102.) To apply, a project must be an in-fill development and meet the following
criteria: (1) is consistent with the applicable General Plan designation and applicable policies,
as well as applicable zoning designations and regulations, (2) would occur on a site less than
five (5) acres, (3) the project site must have no habitat value, (4) the project would not result in
significant traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality effects, and (5) the site can be adequately
served by all required utilities and public services. The Class 32 exemption reflects the
understanding that “the majority of private projects for which a government permit or similar
entitlement is necessary are minor in scope … and hence, in the absence of unusual
circumstances, have little or no effect on the public environment.” (Pacific Palisades Residents
Association, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles (2023) 88 Cal.App.5th 1338, 1363.) If a project meets
the criteria and qualifies for the Class 32 exemption, the project is categorically exempt from
   PC#2887 – 305 Beacon Street
  Page 11

CEQA unless one of the exceptions to exemptions apply. The exemption is not limited to any
use type and may apply to residential, commercial, industrial, public facility, and/or mixed-use
projects.

The project meets all of the aforementioned requirements and is exempt under Class 32, as
supported by substantial evidence:

  a) General Plan and Zoning Consistency: The project site is designated Special Commercial
  (SC) by the General Plan Land Use Element and is located within the SC Zoning District.
  The SC designation provides an area in which both small scale residential and

Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15332 (Class 32 – In-fill Development Projects)
because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.

  1
 The Class 32 reflects a determination by the California Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
that projects that meet the Class 32 criteria will not have a significant environmental effect and,
therefore, are exempt from CEQA. (Berkeley Hillside Preservation v. City of Berkeley (2015) 60
Cal.4th 1086, 1102.) To apply, a project must be an in-fill development and meet the following
criteria: (1) is consistent with the applicable General Plan designation and applicable policies, as
well as applicable zoning designations and regulations, (2) would occur on a site less than five (5)
acres, (3) the project site must have no habitat value, (4) the project would not result in significant
traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality effects, and (5) the site can be adequately served by all
required utilities and public services. The Class 32 exemption reflects the understanding that “the
majority of private projects for which a government permit or similar entitlement is necessary are
minor in scope … and hence, in the absence of unusual circumstances, have little or no effect on
the public environment.” (Pacific Palisades Residents Association, Inc. v. City of Los Angeles
(2023) 88 Cal.App.5th 1338, 1363.) If a project meets the criteria and qualifies for the Class 32
exemption, the project is categorically exempt from CEQA unless one of the exceptions to
exemptions apply. The exemption is not limited to any use type and may apply to residential,
commercial, industrial, public facility, and/or mixed-use projects.

Variance:

AMC Chapter 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance
  deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land within the city within
  the development parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall
  community character.

  The applicant is requesting multiple variances from the development standards for the SC
  zone, as follows:

  •  Allow building height of 18 to 30 ft above grade to top of parapet, with an
  additional 10 ft for rooftop bathroom enclosure, 12 feet for elevator tower, and
  16 feet for emergency staircase, where 28 feet is allowed.
  •  Allow 93% lot coverage, where a maximum of 80% is allowed.
  •  Allow 166% floor area, where a maximum of 140% is allowed.

  Though the property is of regular size, the sloped topography of the lot is unusual compared
  to the majority of other properties within the SC zone. The majority of lots within the

  6
   Special Commercial zone, and commercial zoning districts in general, are located within
  the “Flats.” As a result, the development standards have been written to apply to lots with
  flat topography. For instance, the maximum building height in the SC zone is 28 feet. The
  municipal code definition for building height is “…the vertical distance from the lot's
  natural surface to the highest point of the building.” (AMC Section 9-3.608). Other zones
  in the c0ity, particularly the residential zones, have additional detailed standards for
  measurement of building height (low slope, hillside, steep hillside) that account for the
  topography present within the zone to allow for equitable development of all lots. However,
  in the case of a sloped lot in the SC zone, strict application of the definition of building
  height would mean that the actual buildable area of the lot would be substantially less on a
  sloped lot than a flat lot, which would deprive the property of the same development
  potential compared to other properties within the same zone.

  Therefore, the proposed variances may be granted in conformance with the findings of the
  municipal code, as there are special circumstances related to lot topography that would
  otherwise deprive the property of the development potential of other lots within the same
  zone that lack the sloped topography of this lot.

2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  The requested variances are consistent with approved development of other properties with

3. A variance shall not be granted for a parcel of property which authorizes a use or

  employees. The applicant has estimated that one full-time employee will be employed
